verdict.rationale: Unstructured documents a first-party Transform MCP server and a quickstart for going from a source file to structured output 'with Claude and plain language prompts', so natural-language operation is an officially supported path. However, the language understanding comes from an external AI client (Claude, Cursor, etc.). The documented scope is mainly having Transform ingest local files and output partitioned, enriched, chunked, and embedded data. missing for 10: a built-in natural-language interface within the product itself, evidence that natural-language commands cover workflow, connector, and job management beyond local-file transforms, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Use Unstructured with Claude and plain language prompts to go from an unstructured source file to structured data output in about 5 minutes.

The Transform MCP server enables you to link your AI tools to Transform. You can then use your AI tools to have Transform ingest your local files and output the results as partitioned, enriched, chunked, and embedded data, ready for your immediate use.
When you are deciding which MCP server, SDK, or API to use, prefer this order of priority: 1. MCP server: Unstructured Transform MCP server
